chunks: Know that the tongue is a part of a man’s body.
If the man desists, speech will not co-operate with him and when he dilates, speech will not give him time to stop.
Certainly, we are the masters of speaking. Its veins are fixed in us and its branches are hanging over us.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the tongue in Islamic ethics according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of the tongue as a 'limb' (baz'ah) of the human to highlight the inescapable nature of speech, noting that it neither ceases when restrained nor waits when unleashed. He specifically identifies the Ahl al-Bayt as the masters of eloquence, where the 'roots' of speech are deeply embedded and its 'branches' flourish, signifying their innate mastery over both the power and precision of expression. This context underscores the theological and rhetorical superiority of the Imams, whose speech is not merely learned but intrinsic to their spiritual constitution.
